## Overview

**Core question:** Does the Vulkan CTS execute declarative GLSL shader-library cases with the intended shader stages, values, and output checks?

- This page covers the `ShaderLibraryGroup` implementation in [`vktShaderLibrary.cpp`](../../../modules/vulkan/vktShaderLibrary.cpp#L1689-L1829) and its registered users under the `glsl` test category.
- [`createGlslTests()`](../../../modules/vulkan/vktTestPackage.cpp#L1215-L1251) registers nine ES310 data files—`arrays`, `conditionals`, `constant_expressions`, `constants`, `conversions`, `functions`, `linkage`, `scoping`, and `swizzles`—plus `440.linkage`.
- Each `.test` file supplies declarative groups and cases. The shared parser builds the hierarchy, while the Vulkan factory turns parsed cases into executable `ShaderCase` instances.
- The runner specializes vertex-only, fragment-only, complete, and value-driven cases, renders a `64 x 64` target, and checks the copied-back pixels.

## Background Knowledge

- A GLSL shader-library case describes program stages and expected values declaratively. `group` blocks organize test cases; `case` blocks provide shader source, values, requirements, and optional output mode. This distinction matters because the registered hierarchy is partly generated by parsing data files rather than hard-coded in the Vulkan source.
- A complete graphics case links the outputs written by the vertex stage to the inputs consumed by the fragment stage. The `linkage` data files deliberately exercise declarations, component layouts, and legal type relationships, so both stage interfaces must be understood when interpreting a result.
- A rendered result is copied from a Vulkan image to host-visible memory before the test decides pass or fail. Shader-side `OUTPUT_RESULT` cases encode comparison success as white pixels; `OUTPUT_COLOR` cases encode expected values directly in the color attachment.

## Registration Hierarchy

```text
glsl
├── arrays
├── conditionals
├── constant_expressions
├── constants
├── conversions
├── functions
├── linkage
├── scoping
├── swizzles
└── 440
```

The `440` intermediate node contains the registered `linkage` test family. The direct ES310 test families are created from `s_es310Tests[]`; the `440` group and its `linkage` child are created from `s_440Tests[]` in [`createGlslTests()`](../../../modules/vulkan/vktTestPackage.cpp#L1219-L1251). The tree above intentionally excludes later non-library `glsl` families registered after the shader-library block.

## Behavior Parameters

The primary behavioral axis is the registered shader-library test family or, within a family, its declarative group and case path. The source files define the complete case matrix; representative values below show how that axis changes behavior.

### ES310 language-feature families — distinct GLSL properties

`arrays` checks array declarations, constructors, indexing, `length()`, return values, parameters, and related legal or illegal forms. `conditionals`, `constant_expressions`, `constants`, `conversions`, `functions`, `scoping`, and `swizzles` apply the same parser-and-runner mechanism to their respective GLSL language rules. The family names are registered exactly in [`s_es310Tests[]`](../../../modules/vulkan/vktTestPackage.cpp#L1220-L1233), while their concrete groups and cases come from the corresponding `.test` files.

### `linkage` — ES310 varying interfaces

The ES310 `linkage` family checks vertex/fragment interface declarations and legal interface relationships. Its `varying.rules` cases include `vertex_declare`, `both_declare`, and legal vector-component mismatches such as `legal_mismatch_vec4_vec3`; each case supplies explicit `vertex` and `fragment` blocks in [`linkage.test`](../../../data/vulkan/glsl/es310/linkage.test#L3-L80). The parser creates one complete case when explicit stage sources are present and no pipeline-program list is used ([`parseShaderCase()`](../../../../../framework/opengl/gluShaderLibrary.cpp#L1612-L1632)).

### `440.linkage` — component-qualified interfaces

The `440.linkage` family tests core-GLSL component-qualified vertex inputs and related varying layouts. For example, `varying.component.vert_in.vec2.as_float_float` reads two component-qualified scalar inputs, adds them, and emits a `vec2`; its `output_color vec2` declaration makes the expected vector a direct color result ([`linkage.test`](../../../data/vulkan/glsl/440/linkage.test#L3-L45)). Other cases vary vector width, component placement, and whether an unused component is read.

### `both` cases — two generated stage variants

A `both` shader block is not one executable case. The parser creates `<case>_vertex` and `<case>_fragment`; the Vulkan implementation combines the supplied stage with a generated counterpart in [`ShaderCase::initPrograms()`](../../../modules/vulkan/vktShaderLibrary.cpp#L1716-L1731). This matters for families such as `arrays`, where one shader body is intentionally exercised in both stage roles.

### Value sets — repeated sub-cases

Each value alternative selects one input/reference/uniform arrangement. The runner writes the selected values to host-visible buffers, submits the same graphics work, and repeats until all output-derived sub-cases have been checked ([`ShaderCaseInstance::iterate()`](../../../modules/vulkan/vktShaderLibrary.cpp#L1607-L1686)).

## Shader Analysis

Shader-library behavior is defined by generated or embedded GLSL rather than by one fixed shader. A representative `arrays` case uses the `both` form and an array constructor:

```glsl
float[3] x;
x = float[3] (in0.z, in0.x, in0.y);
out0 = vec3(x[0], x[1], x[2]);
```

The `${DECLARATIONS}`, `${SETUP}`, and `${OUTPUT}` substitutions connect this body to generated input/reference declarations and the selected output mode. The parser emits `<case>_vertex` and `<case>_fragment`; the Vulkan layer then supplies the missing stage with `genVertexShader()` or `genFragmentShader()` ([`parseShaderCase()`](../../../../../framework/opengl/gluShaderLibrary.cpp#L1570-L1610), [`ShaderCase::initPrograms()`](../../../modules/vulkan/vktShaderLibrary.cpp#L1716-L1731)).

For explicit-stage `linkage` cases, the important shader contract is the interface between declarations such as `layout(location = 0) out ... var` in the vertex shader and the matching `layout(location = 0) in ... var` in the fragment shader. The ES310 data file includes both unused declarations and legal width mismatches, while the 440 data file adds `component` qualifiers to vertex inputs ([`es310/linkage.test`](../../../data/vulkan/glsl/es310/linkage.test#L3-L80), [`440/linkage.test`](../../../data/vulkan/glsl/440/linkage.test#L3-L45)).

The generated fragment comparison uses `isOk(value, reference, 0.05)` for floating-point outputs and exact `isOk(value, reference)` for non-floating outputs ([`genCompareOp()`](../../../modules/vulkan/vktShaderLibrary.cpp#L206-L237)). In `OUTPUT_RESULT` mode it writes a white fragment only when all selected outputs compare successfully.

## Runtime Execution and Result Checking

- `ShaderLibraryGroup::init()` lazily parses its stored `.test` filename with a `ShaderCaseFactory`, then attaches the resulting groups and cases ([`ShaderLibraryGroup::init()`](../../../modules/vulkan/vktShaderLibrary.cpp#L1790-L1817)).
- `ShaderCase::initPrograms()` validates the specification and supports only `EXPECT_PASS`. Vertex-only and fragment-only cases receive generated counterpart stages; complete cases specialize all supplied program sources ([`ShaderCase::initPrograms()`](../../../modules/vulkan/vktShaderLibrary.cpp#L1707-L1759)).
- `ShaderCaseInstance` creates input, reference, and uniform buffers when needed, a `64 x 64` render target, readback buffers, a graphics pipeline, descriptors, and a command buffer ([`ShaderCaseInstance`](../../../modules/vulkan/vktShaderLibrary.cpp#L1227-L1291)).
- Before each iteration, selected values are copied into the input, reference, and uniform allocations and CPU writes are flushed. The command buffer is submitted and waited on before readback ([`writeValuesToMem()`](../../../modules/vulkan/vktShaderLibrary.cpp#L1218-L1225), [`iterate()`](../../../modules/vulkan/vktShaderLibrary.cpp#L1607-L1623)).
- In `OUTPUT_RESULT`, every pixel must be `(255, 255, 255, 255)`. In `OUTPUT_COLOR`, every pixel in each output attachment must equal the reference vector assembled from the current output values ([`checkResultImage()`](../../../modules/vulkan/vktShaderLibrary.cpp#L1574-L1590), [`checkResultImageWithReference()`](../../../modules/vulkan/vktShaderLibrary.cpp#L1592-L1605)).
- A failing image returns `TestStatus::fail()` and reports the sub-case; otherwise the runner returns `incomplete()` until all value sets finish, then returns pass ([`iterate()`](../../../modules/vulkan/vktShaderLibrary.cpp#L1624-L1686)).

## Failure Meaning

### Failure Cause Mapping

| If this behavior parameter value fails | Possible failure cause(s) |
|---|---|
| An ES310 language-feature family or case | The implementation did not compile, link, execute, or produce the expected result for that GLSL feature. |
| `linkage` interface case | Vertex/fragment interface handling or the case's expected linkage behavior produced a mismatching image. |
| `440.linkage` component case | Core-GLSL component-qualified input mapping or the arithmetic/output path produced a mismatching color. |
| A `both`-derived `_vertex` or `_fragment` case | The supplied stage or the generated counterpart stage was not specialized or executed as required. |
| Any value-set sub-case | The selected inputs, uniforms, expected outputs, or repeated sub-case handling did not produce the expected pixels. |

### Cause Analysis

#### Shader compilation or specialization

**Possible failure symptoms:** The case fails before a valid rendered result is available, or a shader-generated result is consistently wrong for a case whose source is otherwise valid.

**Possible implementation causes:** The Vulkan source specializes the declarative stage form incorrectly, mishandles required extensions, or the shader compiler rejects or lowers the GLSL construct contrary to the case's intended semantics. The inspected source establishes these execution paths but does not identify a particular implementation defect.

#### Stage linkage and component mapping

**Possible failure symptoms:** `linkage` or `440.linkage` cases report non-white or nonmatching pixels while other cases can execute.

**Possible implementation causes:** Vertex-to-fragment interface matching, component-qualified input mapping, or legal type-width handling may differ from the behavior exercised by the case. The concrete source and validation logic support this interpretation; locating the defect requires source-level investigation of the implementation involved.

#### Value transfer or result checking

**Possible failure symptoms:** A specific sub-case fails with invalid pixels, and the log identifies its sub-case or output attachment.

**Possible implementation causes:** Host-written values, reference data, shader comparison, rendering, image-to-buffer copyback, invalidation, or host-side pixel comparison may disagree. The CTS source confirms each stage of this path, but a failing result alone does not identify which stage is responsible.

## Case Pruning

### Requirement-based pruning

- Cases with unsupported or unsatisfied extension, capability, limit, or GLSL-support requirements are filtered according to the parser and Vulkan test framework's requirement handling. The parser accepts extension alternatives, limits, and support directives in [`parseRequirement()`](../../../../../framework/opengl/gluShaderLibrary.cpp#L1220-L1303).
- Invalid case shapes are rejected by shared validation, including incompatible stage combinations and incomplete complete cases ([`isValid()`](../../../../../framework/opengl/gluShaderLibrary.cpp#L210-L224)).
- The Vulkan wrapper rejects `expect` values other than `EXPECT_PASS` ([`ShaderCase::initPrograms()`](../../../modules/vulkan/vktShaderLibrary.cpp#L1707-L1715)).

### Design-based pruning

- A `both` block is deliberately expanded into two stage-specific cases rather than retained as a single mixed-stage case ([`parseShaderCase()`](../../../../../framework/opengl/gluShaderLibrary.cpp#L1570-L1610)).
- The page does not enumerate every generated descendant: nested groups, cases, and imported files are data-file-defined and can expand the registered matrix beyond the direct roots shown above.

## Key Takeaways

- `vktShaderLibrary.cpp` is shared execution infrastructure; the `.test` files define the concrete GLSL language and linkage cases.
- Registration has two forms: nine direct ES310 shader-library families and `440.linkage` below the explicit `440` intermediate node.
- The same declarative case can generate separate vertex and fragment variants when it uses `both`.
- Correctness is established by rendering, copying back a `64 x 64` image, and checking either white success pixels or exact expected output colors.
- A failure identifies a mismatch in the tested shader behavior or execution path, but the result check alone does not localize the implementation cause.
